meanings.note: in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

examples.text: Уважаемый ветеран, перед вами внук предателя!
examples.trans: Esteemed veteran, before you is the grandson of a traitor!

meanings.note: Core Russian name meaning 'Igor' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Знакомьтесь, Игорь теперь ваш новый главный хозяин.
examples.trans: Meet Igor, he is now your new main owner.

examples.text: Игорь Валентинович сказал, что в ресторане установили камеры.
examples.trans: Igor Valentinovich said they installed cameras at the restaurant.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Я прекрасно понимаю = I understand perfectly

examples.text: Нет, лучше так: все говорят, а я делаю! Прекрасно.
examples.trans: No, better like this: everyone talks, while I do! Excellent.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to look, appear'.

examples.trans: On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'compliment; complimentary gift' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: complimentary gift from the house (in restaurants/services)

examples.text: Это небольшой комплимент от нашего заведения.
examples.trans: This is a small gift from our establishment.
He paid her a nice compliment.
And I will take care of an important compliment.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

стараться.gloss: to try, to make an effort

meanings.en: to try hard, to make an effort
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тараться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try, to make an effort', paired with 'постараться'.

examples.trans: He always tries to help his friends.

examples.text: Марина, зря вы стараетесь. Он никогда не уйдёт от своей Аллы Евгеньевны.
examples.trans: Marina, you're trying in vain. He will never leave his Alla Evgenyevna.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

examples.text: Плохой бетон привезли. Самсон, ты зря радиаторы носил.
examples.trans: They've delivered bad concrete. Samson, you carried those radiators for nothing.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трогий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strict, stern').

examples.trans: How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

examples.text: У нас в школе очень строгий директор.
examples.trans: We have a very strict principal at our school.

examples.text: Ой, спина не разгибается! Какая вы строгая, Клавдия Викторовна.
examples.trans: Ow, my back won't straighten! How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.
This is my wedding suit, actually!

meanings.note: verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оревнование'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'competition, contest' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Значит, для вас это как соревнование?
examples.trans: So for you this is like a competition?

examples.text: Это слово «соревнование» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'competition' is often heard in conversation.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'даваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give up, to surrender', paired with 'сдаться'.

examples.text: Никогда не сдавайся! Сегодня я выйду отсюда под подписку!
examples.trans: Never give up! Today I'm getting out of here on a travel ban!

examples.text: Я устал, потому что много работал.
examples.trans: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
I'm at home because I'm ill.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'порить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to argue, to dispute', paired with 'поспорить'.

examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue.

examples.text: Это кошмар, я не спорю. Но зачем на видео снимать?
examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue. But why film it on video?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'дачный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('successful, lucky').

examples.trans: This trip will definitely be successful.

examples.text: Тогда эта поездка точно будет удачной.
examples.trans: Then this trip will definitely be successful.
Wonderful, the evening promises to be successful!
